docs.title: nyx-bridge
docs.text:
TCP bridge between Nyx and external processes such as Blender, Maya or any Python interpreter.

Nyx runs a BridgeServer. The external process runs a NyxClient, connects out to the server and executes the code the server sends. The side that runs code never accepts connections. The package uses the standard library only and supports Python 3.11+, so it can be installed into the Python of a DCC.

# in Blender, Maya, mayapy, a script ...
from nyx_bridge.client import NyxClient

NyxClient().serve_forever()  # address from NYX_BRIDGE_ADDRESS / NYX_BRIDGE_TOKEN

# in Nyx (or any Python)
from nyx_bridge.server import BridgeServer

with BridgeServer() as server:
    session = server.wait_for_client(timeout=30)
    print(session.execute("result = 6 * 7").value)   # 42
If you want to... Read Connect an application to Nyx, or run code in one User Guide Work on nyx-bridge, or on a client for a new application Developer Guide Look up a class or function API reference (see the navigation)

Ready-made clients: nyx-bridge-maya and nyx-bridge-blender.

docs.title: client
docs.text:
Base client connecting an application to a running Nyx.

Standard library only, for Python 3.11+: clients live inside other applications (DCCs) that install this package without Nyx or Qt.

Subclass NyxClient for an application: fill default_namespace (e.g. with bpy) and, if the application is not safe to touch from other threads, override run_on_main_thread.

docs.title: NyxClient(name=None, address=None, token=None, reconnect=True, reconnect_delay=1.0)
docs.text:
Connects to a Nyx bridge server and runs the code it sends.

Two ways to run it:

  • serve_forever blocks the calling thread, which is then the thread executing the code. Meant for applications run in batch mode, where no event loop exists.
  • start_in_thread serves from a background thread and hands every execution to run_on_main_thread, which a subclass implements for its application.

Code runs in a namespace that persists for the lifetime of a connection, so variables of one execution are visible to the next. A script exposes its return value by assigning result.

def __init__(
    self,
    name: str | None = None,
    address: str | tuple[str, int] | None = None,
    token: str | None = None,
    reconnect: bool = True,
    reconnect_delay: float = 1.0,
) -> None:
    """Initialize NyxClient.

    Args:
        name (str | None): name shown by the server. Derived from the kind and the
            process id if omitted.
        address (str | tuple[str, int] | None): `host:port` of the server. The
            environment is used if omitted, see `protocol.find_server_address`.
        token (str | None): server token, from the environment if omitted.
        reconnect (bool): connect again when the connection drops.
        reconnect_delay (float): seconds between connection attempts.
    """
    self.name = name or f"{self.CLIENT_KIND}-{os.getpid()}"
    self._address = address
    self._token = token
    self._reconnect = reconnect
    self._reconnect_delay = reconnect_delay
    self._stop_event = threading.Event()
    self._sock: socket.socket | None = None
    self._namespace: dict[str, typing.Any] = {}
    self.client_id: str | None = None
    self.server_name: str | None = None

def connect(self) -> None:
    """Open one connection and handshake.

    Raises:
        ConnectionError: nothing says where the server is.
        OSError: the server can't be reached.
        protocol.HandshakeError: the server refused the hello.
        protocol.ProtocolError: the server broke the protocol.
    """
    address = protocol.find_server_address(self._address, self._token)
    if address is None:
        raise ConnectionError(
            f"Unknown Nyx server address, set {protocol.ADDRESS_ENV_VAR}"
        )
    sock = socket.create_connection(
        (address.host, address.port), timeout=self.HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT
    )
    try:
        protocol.send_message(
            sock,
            protocol.make_hello(
                address.token,
                self.name,
                self.CLIENT_KIND,
                self.client_version(),
            ),
        )
        reply = protocol.recv_message(sock)
        if reply["type"] == protocol.MessageType.ERROR:
            raise protocol.HandshakeError(reply.get("message", "Refused"))
        if reply["type"] != protocol.MessageType.ACK:
            raise protocol.ProtocolError(f"Unexpected reply: {reply['type']}")
        sock.settimeout(None)
    except BaseException:
        sock.close()
        raise

    self.client_id = reply.get("client_id")
    self.server_name = reply.get("server_name")
    self._namespace = dict(self.default_namespace())
    self._namespace.setdefault("__name__", "__nyx__")
    self._sock = sock
    LOGGER.info("Connected to %s as %s", self.server_name, self.name)
    self.on_connected()

def execute(
    self,
    code: str,
    mode: str = protocol.EXEC,
    args: dict | None = None,
    request_id: str | None = None,
) -> dict:
    """Run code in the persistent namespace. Never raises.

    Output written to stdout and stderr while it runs is captured. In `exec` mode
    the value is what the code assigned to `result`, in `eval` mode the value of
    the expression.

    Args:
        code (str): source to run.
        mode (str): `protocol.EXEC` or `protocol.EVAL`.
        args (dict | None): names to set in the namespace before running.
        request_id (str | None): id of the request being answered.

    Returns:
        dict: result message, see `protocol.make_result`.
    """
    namespace = self._namespace
    namespace.update(args or {})
    stdout, stderr = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()
    value, error, ok = None, None, True
    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(stdout), contextlib.redirect_stderr(stderr):
        try:
            if mode == protocol.EVAL:
                value = eval(compile(code, "<nyx>", "eval"), namespace)
            elif mode == protocol.EXEC:
                namespace.pop("result", None)
                exec(compile(code, "<nyx>", "exec"), namespace)
                value = namespace.get("result")
            else:
                raise ValueError(f"Unknown execution mode: {mode!r}")
        except (Exception, SystemExit) as err:
            ok, error = False, self._describe_error(err)
    return protocol.make_result(
        request_id,
        ok,
        value=protocol.to_jsonable(value),
        error=error,
        stdout=stdout.getvalue(),
        stderr=stderr.getvalue(),
    )

def serve_forever(self, connect_timeout: float | None = None) -> None:
    """Connect and run what the server sends, until stopped or told to shut down.

    Reconnects when the connection drops (if enabled). Runs on the calling thread.

    Args:
        connect_timeout (float | None): seconds to keep trying to reach the
            server, per attempt to connect. Forever if omitted.

    Raises:
        ConnectionError: the server was not reached within `connect_timeout`.
        protocol.HandshakeError: the server refused this client, retrying would
            not help.
    """
    self._stop_event.clear()
    while not self._stop_event.is_set():
        self._connect_with_retry(connect_timeout)
        if not self.is_connected:
            break  # stopped while trying to connect
        try:
            # `stop` may have come in between connecting and here, when it had
            # no connection to close yet.
            if not self._stop_event.is_set():
                self._serve_connection()
        finally:
            self._close_socket()
            self.on_disconnected()
        if not self._reconnect:
            break

def start_in_thread(self, connect_timeout: float | None = None) -> threading.Thread:
    """Serve from a daemon thread.

    Args:
        connect_timeout (float | None): see `serve_forever`.

    Returns:
        threading.Thread: running thread.
    """
    thread = threading.Thread(
        target=self.serve_forever,
        args=(connect_timeout,),
        name=f"NyxClient-{self.name}",
        daemon=True,
    )
    thread.start()
    return thread

docs.title: protocol
docs.text:
Wire protocol shared by the Nyx bridge server and its clients.

Standard library only, for Python 3.11+: clients living in other applications (DCCs) install this package, so it must have no dependencies.

Messages are JSON objects with a type key, sent over TCP with a 4-byte big-endian length prefix.

docs.text:
Where Nyx writes its address file unless told otherwise.

The folder is the per-user data folder of the Nyx application, so a client on the same machine finds a running Nyx without any configuration.

Returns:

Type Description Path

pathlib.Path: path of the file, which may not exist.

Source code in src/nyx_bridge/protocol.py 
def default_address_file_path() -> pathlib.Path:
    """Where Nyx writes its address file unless told otherwise.

    The folder is the per-user data folder of the Nyx application, so a client on
    the same machine finds a running Nyx without any configuration.

    Returns:
        pathlib.Path: path of the file, which may not exist.
    """
    if sys.platform == "darwin":
        base = pathlib.Path.home() / "Library" / "Application Support" / "nyx"
    elif sys.platform == "win32":
        local = os.environ.get("LOCALAPPDATA") or pathlib.Path.home() / "AppData/Local"
        base = pathlib.Path(local) / "sowwic" / "nyx"
    else:
        data = os.environ.get("XDG_DATA_HOME") or pathlib.Path.home() / ".local/share"
        base = pathlib.Path(data) / "nyx"
    return base / DEFAULT_ADDRESS_FILE_NAME

def encode_message(message: dict) -> bytes:
    """Serialize a message and prefix it with its length.

    Args:
        message (dict): JSON serializable message.

    Raises:
        TypeError: message can't be serialized to JSON.
        ProtocolError: message is larger than `MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE`.

    Returns:
        bytes: frame to send.
    """
    payload = json.dumps(message, separators=(",", ":")).encode("utf-8")
    if len(payload) > MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE:
        raise ProtocolError(f"Message too large: {len(payload)} bytes")
    return _HEADER.pack(len(payload)) + payload

def find_server_address(
    address: str | tuple[str, int] | None = None, token: str | None = None
) -> Address | None:
    """Work out where the server is.

    Looked up in order: the arguments, `NYX_BRIDGE_ADDRESS` (`host:port`) with
    `NYX_BRIDGE_TOKEN`, then the file named by `NYX_BRIDGE_ADDRESS_FILE`, then the
    default address file of a running Nyx (see `default_address_file_path`).

    Args:
        address (str | tuple[str, int] | None): `host:port` or (host, port).
        token (str | None): token, taken from the environment if omitted.

    Returns:
        Address | None: None when nothing says where the server is.
    """
    if address is None:
        address = os.environ.get(ADDRESS_ENV_VAR)
    if address:
        if isinstance(address, str):
            host, port = parse_address(address)
        else:
            host, port = address
        if token is None:
            token = os.environ.get(TOKEN_ENV_VAR, "")
        return Address(host, int(port), token)

    candidates = [os.environ.get(ADDRESS_FILE_ENV_VAR), default_address_file_path()]
    for address_file in candidates:
        if address_file and os.path.isfile(address_file):
            found = read_address_file(address_file)
            return found if token is None else found._replace(token=token)
    return None

def parse_address(text: str) -> tuple[str, int]:
    """Split `host:port`.

    Args:
        text (str): address, a bare port means the default host.

    Raises:
        ValueError: text is not an address.

    Returns:
        tuple[str, int]: host and port.
    """
    host, separator, port = text.strip().rpartition(":")
    if not separator:
        host, port = DEFAULT_HOST, text.strip()
    return host or DEFAULT_HOST, int(port)

def recv_message(sock: socket.socket) -> dict:
    """Block until a whole message is read.

    Args:
        sock (socket.socket): connected socket.

    Raises:
        ConnectionClosed: connection closed or broken.
        ProtocolError: invalid frame, size or payload.
        TimeoutError: socket timeout expired.

    Returns:
        dict: message.
    """
    (size,) = _HEADER.unpack(_recv_exact(sock, _HEADER.size))
    if size > MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE:
        raise ProtocolError(f"Message too large: {size} bytes")
    payload = _recv_exact(sock, size)
    try:
        message = json.loads(payload.decode("utf-8"))
    except ValueError as err:
        raise ProtocolError(f"Invalid message payload: {err}") from err
    if not isinstance(message, dict) or not isinstance(message.get("type"), str):
        raise ProtocolError("Message has to be an object with a string `type`")
    return message

def to_jsonable(value: typing.Any, _depth: int = 0) -> typing.Any:
    """Convert a value to something JSON can carry.

    Containers are converted item by item. Anything else that JSON can't carry, like
    an object of the application, becomes its `repr`.

    Args:
        value (Any): value to convert.

    Returns:
        Any: JSON serializable value.
    """
    if value is None or isinstance(value, (bool, int, float, str)):
        return value
    if _depth < _MAX_JSON_DEPTH:
        if isinstance(value, (list, tuple, set, frozenset)):
            return [to_jsonable(item, _depth + 1) for item in value]
        if isinstance(value, dict):
            return {
                str(key): to_jsonable(item, _depth + 1) for key, item in value.items()
            }
    try:
        return repr(value)
    except Exception:
        return f"<unrepresentable {type(value).__name__}>"

def write_address_file(
    path: str | os.PathLike, host: str, port: int, token: str
) -> None:
    """Write where a server listens, so clients on the machine can find it.

    The file holds the token, so it is made readable by the owner only where possible.

docs.title: server
docs.text:
Server side of the Nyx bridge: accepts clients and sends them code to run.

Everything here runs on plain threads and standard library sockets, no Qt. The crawler is synchronous, so a request just blocks its caller until the client answers. Never touch stage objects from the threads of this module.

def __init__(
    self,
    name: str | None = None,
    host: str = protocol.DEFAULT_HOST,
    port: int | None = None,
    token: str | None = None,
    address_file: str | os.PathLike | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Initialize BridgeServer.

    Args:
        name (str | None): server name, the class name if omitted.
        host (str): interface to listen on. Keep it local: clients can have code
            run on them by whoever holds the token.
        port (int | None): port to listen on. None tries `DEFAULT_PORT` and the
            ports after it, 0 lets the system choose, anything else is used as is.
        token (str | None): shared secret clients have to present, random if
            omitted.
        address_file (str | os.PathLike | None): file that tells clients where
            the server is. Written when the server starts and removed when it
            stops.
    """
    self.address_file = address_file
    self.name = name or type(self).__name__
    self.host = host
    self.token = token or secrets.token_urlsafe(16)
    self._requested_port = port
    self._listener: socket.socket | None = None
    self._accept_thread: threading.Thread | None = None
    self._stop_event = threading.Event()
    self._clients: list[ClientSession] = []
    self._condition = threading.Condition()
    self._listeners: list[typing.Any] = []
    self._port = port
    if host not in ("127.0.0.1", "localhost", "::1"):
        LOGGER.warning("Bridge server %s is listening on %s", self.name, host)

docs.title: add_listener(listener)
docs.text:
Get told about what happens to the server.

A listener is any object with some of these methods, the others are skipped: on_server_started(server), on_server_stopped(server), on_client_connected(server, session) and on_client_disconnected(server, session).

They are called on the threads of the server, not on the one that added the listener, so they have to be quick and thread safe. A failing listener is logged and does not affect the server or the other listeners.

Name Type Description Default listener Any

object to call, ignored if it is already added.

def add_listener(self, listener: typing.Any) -> None:
    """Get told about what happens to the server.

    A listener is any object with some of these methods, the others are skipped:
    `on_server_started(server)`, `on_server_stopped(server)`,
    `on_client_connected(server, session)` and
    `on_client_disconnected(server, session)`.

    They are called on the threads of the server, not on the one that added the
    listener, so they have to be quick and thread safe. A failing listener is
    logged and does not affect the server or the other listeners.

    Args:
        listener (Any): object to call, ignored if it is already added.
    """
    with self._condition:
        if listener not in self._listeners:
            self._listeners.append(listener)

def start(self) -> None:
    """Start listening and accepting clients.

    Raises:
        OSError: no port could be bound.
    """
    if self.is_running:
        return
    self._listener = self._bind()
    self._port = self._listener.getsockname()[1]
    self._stop_event.clear()
    self._accept_thread = threading.Thread(
        target=self._accept_loop, name=f"BridgeServer-{self.name}", daemon=True
    )
    self._accept_thread.start()
    if self.address_file is not None:
        self._write_own_address_file()
    LOGGER.info(
        "Bridge server %s listening on %s:%s", self.name, self.host, self.port
    )
    self._notify("on_server_started")

docs.title: stop()
docs.text:
Stop listening and disconnect every client.

Source code in src/nyx_bridge/server.py 
def stop(self) -> None:
    """Stop listening and disconnect every client."""
    if not self.is_running:
        return
    self._stop_event.set()
    listener, self._listener = self._listener, None
    listener.close()
    if self._accept_thread is not None:
        self._accept_thread.join(timeout=2)
        self._accept_thread = None
    for session in self.clients:
        session.close()
    with self._condition:
        self._condition.notify_all()
    if self.address_file is not None:
        self._remove_own_address_file()
    LOGGER.info("Bridge server %s stopped", self.name)
    self._notify("on_server_stopped")

def wait_for_client(
    self,
    name: str | None = None,
    kind: str | None = None,
    client_id: str | None = None,
    timeout: float | None = None,
) -> ClientSession:
    """Wait until a matching client is connected.

    Args:
        name (str | None): client name.
        kind (str | None): client kind.
        client_id (str | None): client id.
        timeout (float | None): seconds to wait, forever if None.

    Raises:
        TimeoutError: no matching client within the timeout.
        RuntimeError: the server was stopped while waiting.

    Returns:
        ClientSession: first matching client.
    """

    def find() -> ClientSession | None:
        matches = [
            session
            for session in self._clients
            if (name is None or session.name == name)
            and (kind is None or session.kind == kind)
            and (client_id is None or session.id == client_id)
        ]
        return matches[0] if matches else None

    with self._condition:
        self._condition.wait_for(
            lambda: find() is not None or self._stop_event.is_set(), timeout
        )
        session = find()
    if session is not None:
        return session
    if self._stop_event.is_set():
        raise RuntimeError(f"Bridge server {self.name} was stopped")
    raise TimeoutError(
        f"No client (name={name!r}, kind={kind!r}) connected to {self.name} "
        f"within {timeout}s"
    )

def __init__(
    self,
    sock: socket.socket,
    client_id: str,
    name: str,
    kind: str,
    version: str,
    address: tuple,
) -> None:
    """Initialize ClientSession.

    Args:
        sock (socket.socket): connection, already handshaken.
        client_id (str): id given to the client by the server.
        name (str): client name.
        kind (str): client kind, e.g. "blender".
        version (str): client application version.
        address (tuple): remote address of the connection.
    """
    self._sock = sock
    self._send_lock = threading.Lock()
    self._pending_lock = threading.Lock()
    self._pending: dict[str, concurrent.futures.Future] = {}
    self._request_ids = itertools.count(1)
    self._closed = threading.Event()
    self.id = client_id
    self.name = name
    self.kind = kind
    self.version = version
    self.address = address

docs.title: close()
docs.text:
Drop the connection. Pending requests fail with ClientDisconnected.

Source code in src/nyx_bridge/server.py 
def close(self) -> None:
    """Drop the connection. Pending requests fail with `ClientDisconnected`."""
    if self._closed.is_set():
        return
    self._closed.set()
    try:
        self._sock.shutdown(socket.SHUT_RDWR)
    except OSError:
        pass
    self._sock.close()
    with self._pending_lock:
        pending, self._pending = self._pending, {}
    for future in pending.values():
        if not future.done():
            future.set_exception(ClientDisconnected(f"{self.name} disconnected"))

def execute(
    self,
    code: str,
    args: dict | None = None,
    mode: str = protocol.EXEC,
    timeout: float | None = None,
) -> ExecutionResult:
    """Run code in the client and wait for the answer.

    Args:
        code (str): source to run.
        args (dict | None): names to set in the client's namespace first, has to
            be JSON serializable.
        mode (str): `protocol.EXEC`, the value is what the code assigned to
            `result`, or `protocol.EVAL`, the value of the expression.
        timeout (float | None): seconds to wait for the answer, forever if None.

    Raises:
        TypeError: args are not JSON serializable.
        ClientDisconnected: the client is gone or went away while waiting.
        TimeoutError: no answer within the timeout.
        RemoteExecutionError: the code raised in the client.

    Returns:
        ExecutionResult: value and output.
    """
    request_id = str(next(self._request_ids))
    frame = protocol.encode_message(
        protocol.make_execute(request_id, code, mode, args)
    )
    reply = self._request(request_id, frame, timeout)
    if not reply.get("ok"):
        raise RemoteExecutionError(
            reply.get("error") or {},
            reply.get("stdout", ""),
            reply.get("stderr", ""),
        )
    return ExecutionResult(
        reply.get("value"), reply.get("stdout", ""), reply.get("stderr", "")
    )

def run(self) -> None:
    """Read messages until the connection ends. Runs on the connection's thread."""
    try:
        while True:
            self._dispatch(protocol.recv_message(self._sock))
    except protocol.ConnectionClosed as err:
        LOGGER.info("%s disconnected: %s", self.name, err)
    except (protocol.ProtocolError, OSError) as err:
        LOGGER.warning("Dropping %s: %s", self.name, err)
    finally:
        self.close()

docs.title: Developer Guide
docs.text: This guide is for people who work on nyx-bridge itself, or write a client for a new application.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
uv sync
make check        # ruff + pytest
make mkdocs       # serve these docs

make help lists every target. Ruff uses a line length of 89 and the E, F and UP rules with target-version = "py311". Docstrings are Google style: the API reference is generated from them.

Important

The package must stay standard library only and work on Python 3.11. Clients are installed into the Python of other applications, where nothing else can be assumed. Don't import a third-party package, and don't use syntax newer than 3.11.

Wire protocol Framing, message types, the handshake and the rules both sides follow. Writing a client What to implement to bring a new application to Nyx. Testing The fixtures and what to cover. Releasing Versions, the changelog, make release and publishing to PyPI. API reference Generated from the docstrings (see the navigation).

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
nyx_bridge
├── protocol.py   framing, message builders, JSON conversion, address lookup
├── client.py     NyxClient: connects out, runs code
└── server.py     BridgeServer, ClientSession: accepts clients, sends code

client.py and server.py both depend on protocol.py and not on each other. A client-only install (inside a DCC) only ever runs protocol and client.

docs.title: Direction of the connection
docs.text: The application that runs code is the one that connects. Nyx listens; Blender or Maya dial in. That way a DCC never opens a port, Nyx never has to find or launch an application, and the DCC can start before or after Nyx and just retry.

docs.title: Server threads
docs.text:
BridgeServer-<name>              accept loop (listener has a 0.2 s timeout to see stop())
 └─ BridgeServer-<name>-connection   one per connection:
      handshake, then ClientSession.run() reading messages until the socket ends
caller threads                    ClientSession.execute / ping, blocking on a Future
  • ClientSession._request registers a concurrent.futures.Future under the request id, sends the frame under a send lock, and waits on the future. The connection thread's _dispatch completes the future when a result, pong or error carrying that id arrives. That is what lets several threads share one session.
  • close() fails every pending future with ClientDisconnected.
  • _condition guards the client list, the listeners and wait_for_client. Listener callbacks are called outside the lock, so a slow listener can't stall the server.
  • Servers hand out ports from DEFAULT_PORT upward (PORT_FALLBACK_COUNT tries) because several Nyx instances may run at once.

docs.title: Client threads
docs.text:
A client has one reading loop, _serve_connection, on whichever thread called serve_forever (the calling thread, or the daemon thread of start_in_thread). For an execute message it calls run_on_main_thread(lambda: self._run_request(message)) and sends the reply. Consequences:

  • Executions are serial: the next message isn't read until the current one finishes.
  • A ping queued behind a long execution is answered late, so a server's ping timeout measures responsiveness, not only liveness.
  • stop() sets an event and shuts the socket down, which unblocks the blocking read.
  • A shutdown message sets the same event, so the client leaves without reconnecting.

docs.title: The execution namespace
docs.text:
NyxClient.execute keeps one dict per connection (_namespace), seeded from default_namespace() and __name__ = "__nyx__", and replaced on reconnect. exec mode pops result before running and reads it afterwards. stdout/stderr are redirected with contextlib.redirect_*, which is process-wide: output of other threads running at the same time can end up in the captured text.

SystemExit is caught together with Exception, so sys.exit() in a script is an error of that request, not the end of the host application. Other BaseExceptions (KeyboardInterrupt) are not caught.

docs.title: Values
docs.text: to_jsonable keeps JSON scalars, turns tuples and sets into lists, dicts into dicts with string keys, and everything else into repr(). Nesting deeper than 32 levels is also turned into a repr, which keeps cyclic structures from recursing forever.

docs.title: Writing a client
docs.text:
A client for a new application is a small subclass of NyxClient. Existing ones to read: nyx-bridge-blender and nyx-bridge-maya.

from nyx_bridge.client import NyxClient


class HoudiniClient(NyxClient):
    CLIENT_KIND = "houdini"

    def client_version(self) -> str:
        import hou
        return hou.applicationVersionString()

    def default_namespace(self) -> dict:
        import hou
        return {"hou": hou}

    def run_on_main_thread(self, func):
        ...

docs.title: Checklist
docs.text:
1. CLIENT_KIND: unique and lowercase; servers filter with it (find_clients(kind=)).
  2. default_namespace: the modules scripts will expect, imported lazily inside the method so importing your package works outside the application.
  3. run_on_main_thread: if the application can't be used from other threads, put the function on a queue drained by the application's own timer or idle callback, and block until it ran. Return its value and re-raise what it raised only if you need to; execute already catches exceptions and builds the error message, so the function passed in never raises for user code.
  4. Where to start it: start_in_thread() from the application's startup (plug-in load, add-on register), stop() from its shutdown. In a headless or batch mode with no event loop, call serve_forever() and skip run_on_main_thread.
  5. Dependencies: install sowwic-nyx-bridge with the application's own Python; keep it the only requirement.

docs.title: Things to watch
docs.text:
• Never block the main thread waiting for the server. start_in_thread keeps the connecting and retrying off it.
  • A request can run for a long time. The client answers nothing else meanwhile (see Architecture), so avoid long executions on a client that has to stay responsive.
  • Cleanup. on_disconnected is the place to drop references to application objects created by scripts. The namespace is replaced on reconnect anyway.
  • Thread safety of captured output. redirect_stdout is process wide.

docs.title: Wire protocol
docs.text: PROTOCOL_VERSION = 1. Everything is in nyx_bridge/protocol.py.

docs.title: Framing
docs.text:
Each message is a JSON object (separators=(",", ":"), UTF-8) preceded by its length as a 4-byte big-endian unsigned integer.

+----------------+---------------------------+
| length (u32 BE)| JSON payload (UTF-8)      |
+----------------+---------------------------+
  • A payload larger than MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE (64 MiB) is refused when encoding (sender) and when reading the header (receiver, before allocating).
  • The payload has to be an object with a string type, else ProtocolError.
  • recv_message raises ConnectionClosed (a ProtocolError) when the peer closes mid-frame and passes TimeoutError through.
  • Sockets shared between threads need a lock around send_message; the server's ClientSession has one, the client sends only from its reading thread.

docs.title: Messages
docs.text:
type Direction Fields hello client → server protocol_version, token, client_name, client_kind, client_version ack server → client protocol_version, client_id, server_name error either message, optional id of the request it answers execute server → client id, code, mode ("exec" or "eval"), args (object) result client → server id, ok, value, error, stdout, stderr ping server → client id pong client → server id shutdown server → client none

result.error is {"type", "message", "traceback"} when ok is false, else null. Builders: make_hello, make_ack, make_error, make_execute, make_result, make_ping, make_pong, make_shutdown.

docs.title: Handshake
docs.text:
client                                   server
  │ ── connect ───────────────────────────▶ │
  │ ── hello(token, kind, name, ...) ─────▶ │  must arrive within HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT (5 s)
  │                                         │  checks, in order: type == hello,
  │                                         │  protocol_version, token (constant time),
  │                                         │  then validate_client(hello)
  │ ◀──── ack(client_id, server_name) ───── │  accepted
  │ ◀──── error(message) ─────────────────  │  refused, connection closed

The client waits up to HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT (10 s) for the reply. An error becomes HandshakeError, which serve_forever does not retry. Network errors and ProtocolError are retried.

docs.title: Requests
docs.text:
Request ids are strings chosen by the sender ("1", "2", ... for executions, "ping-N" for pings). An answer carries the id of its request. An error with an id fails that request on the server; an answer whose id nobody waits for (a timed-out request, say) is dropped silently.

An unknown message type received by the client is answered with an error. One received by the server is logged and ignored.

docs.title: Changing the protocol
docs.text:
• Bump PROTOCOL_VERSION for any change an older peer can't understand. The server refuses other versions in the hello, so mixed versions fail loudly at connect.
  • Adding an optional field to a message needs no bump: peers read fields with .get.
  • The clients (nyx-bridge-maya, nyx-bridge-blender) and Nyx pin a tag of this package, so a change lands in each when its pin moves.

docs.title: Branches and versions
docs.text:
develop is the default and PR branch; main is the release branch. Work on a feature branch named after the GitHub issue.

The version lives in VERSION. make update-version copies it into pyproject.toml (and make build does that first). Add a section for it at the top of CHANGELOG.rst, one bullet per user-visible change with the issue number where there is one.

The packages that depend on nyx-bridge (nyx-bridge-maya, nyx-bridge-blender, Nyx itself) pin a git tag of it, so tag every release vX.Y.Z and move the pins. The tags up to v1.0.0 were built when the distribution was still called nyx-bridge: a dependent that moves to a newer tag has to rename the dependency to sowwic-nyx-bridge in its pyproject.toml (and in [tool.uv.sources]) at the same time.

docs.title: Release
docs.text:
make release VERSION=1.2.3 [RELEASE_TITLE="..."]

Runs the release script of sowwic/gh-workflows: it tags main, pushes, and merges back into develop. The tag triggers .github/workflows/release.yml, which creates the GitHub release from the changelog section and attaches dist/*.

docs.title: Publishing to PyPI
docs.text:
The distribution is called sowwic-nyx-bridge and imports as nyx_bridge. The targets come from the general/pypi module of sowwic/makefiles:

make pypi-publish-dev     # build and upload to TestPyPI
make pypi-publish         # build and upload to PyPI

Both run clean and build first, so only a fresh build is uploaded. uv publish reads the token from UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN, so put it in the environment for the run, not in a file:

UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN=pypi-... make pypi-publish
PyPI TestPyPI Account pypi.org test.pypi.org (separate account and tokens) Token page pypi.org/manage/account/token/ test.pypi.org/manage/account/token/

The first upload needs an account-wide token, since a token for one project can only be made once the project exists. After that, replace it with a project-scoped one.

A published version can't be replaced. To fix a bad release, bump VERSION and publish again; to hide one, yank it on pypi.org (there is no API or make target for it).

Before the first upload, check the build and the page:

make build
uvx twine check dist/*
make pypi-publish-dev
pip install --index-url https://test.pypi.org/simple/ sowwic-nyx-bridge

docs.title: CI
docs.text: Workflows in .github/workflows/ are thin callers of the shared ones in sowwic/gh-workflows: tests (Python matrix on Linux and Windows, then macOS), lint, docs deployment to GitHub Pages and the release. Dependabot opens weekly update PRs against develop for the lockfile and the Actions versions.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
make pytest                                              # everything, with coverage
uv run pytest tests/test_bridge.py::test_ping            # one test
make pytest-pdb                                          # verbose, pdb on failure

Coverage (--cov=nyx_bridge) is on by default. make clean and make pytest-pdb remove test_output/.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text: File Covers tests/test_protocol.py Framing, message builders, to_jsonable, address parsing and files, the lookup order of find_server_address. Plain functions and socket pairs, no threads. tests/test_bridge.py A real server and real clients over loopback: connecting, executing, errors, reconnecting, handshake refusals, listeners, ports, address files.

docs.title: Fixtures (tests/test_bridge.py)
docs.text:
• server: a BridgeServer(port=0) that is stopped afterwards. Port 0 means the system picks a free one, so tests can run in parallel with a running Nyx.
  • make_client(**kwargs): starts a NyxClient thread pointed at the server, with a short reconnect_delay, and stops and joins it at the end.
  • session: a client already connected, as the server sees it.
  • wait_until(predicate): polls for a condition. Use it instead of sleep, since connections happen on other threads.

docs.title: What to cover
docs.text:
• A change to a message or the framing: a test in test_protocol.py, and a bridge test that crosses a real socket.
  • A new failure mode of the connection (refused, closed, timed out): both ends, and that the session or client is usable afterwards.
  • Anything with threads: avoid fixed sleeps, use wait_until or events, and keep the timeouts generous (WAIT = 10). A flaky test here is almost always a missing wait.
  • Python 3.11 compatibility: the project supports 3.11, which .python-version pins for local development. CI uses the default matrix of the shared workflow (3.12 to 3.14), so run make check locally before relying on anything newer.

docs.title: User Guide
docs.text: This guide is for people who connect an application to Nyx, or run code in other processes from Python.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install sowwic-nyx-bridge

Requires Python 3.11+, with no other dependencies. To put it in the Python of a DCC that has no pip of its own, install into a folder on its path:

pip install sowwic-nyx-bridge --target <modules dir>

Until a release is on PyPI, use pip install git+https://github.com/sowwic/nyx-bridge.git.

docs.title: Pages
docs.text: Page What you learn Running code in a process NyxClient: serving, what scripts see, results and errors, reconnecting, subclassing for an application. Sending code from a server BridgeServer and ClientSession: starting, finding clients, executing, timeouts, listeners. Finding the server How a client learns the address and token: arguments, environment, address file.

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text:
Nyx                                    Blender / Maya / Python
┌──────────────┐   client connects out   ┌──────────────┐
│ BridgeServer │ ◀────────────────────── │  NyxClient   │
│              │ ───── execute ────────▶ │  runs code   │
│ ClientSession│ ◀──── result ────────── │              │
└──────────────┘                         └──────────────┘
  1. The server listens on a local port and holds a secret token.
  2. A client connects and opens with a hello carrying the token.
  3. The server sends execute requests; the client runs them and answers with the value and the captured output.

docs.title: Finding the server
docs.text:
A client needs a host, a port and the token. It looks for them in this order and uses the first that answers:

  1. The address (and token) given to NyxClient.
  2. The environment: NYX_BRIDGE_ADDRESS (host:port, or a bare port for the local host) with NYX_BRIDGE_TOKEN.
  3. The file named by NYX_BRIDGE_ADDRESS_FILE.
  4. The default address file of a running Nyx.

If none of them says anything, connect() raises ConnectionError, and serve_forever keeps retrying (until its connect_timeout, if you gave one).

A token passed as an argument replaces the one in an address file. NYX_BRIDGE_TOKEN is only read together with an address from the arguments or NYX_BRIDGE_ADDRESS.

docs.title: The address file
docs.text:
The server writes a small JSON file when it starts, with its host, port and token, and removes it when it stops. On the same machine the client then needs no configuration:

{"host": "127.0.0.1", "port": 47770, "token": "..."}
Platform Default location macOS ~/Library/Application Support/nyx/bridge.json Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\sowwic\nyx\bridge.json Linux $XDG_DATA_HOME/nyx/bridge.json, or ~/.local/share/nyx/bridge.json

A server only writes the file when given address_file=... (Nyx does it for you). server.write_address_file(path) writes one once, on demand. The file is readable by its owner only where the platform allows it. When a server stops it removes the file only if it still describes that server, so a newer server that took the file over keeps it.

From code, protocol.find_server_address(), read_address_file() and default_address_file_path() do the same lookups.

docs.title: Several machines, containers
docs.text:
The server listens on 127.0.0.1 by default, so a remote client can't reach it. To allow that, pass another host, set the token yourself, and put both in the client's environment. Do this only on a network you trust: the token is the only protection, and traffic is not encrypted.

export NYX_BRIDGE_ADDRESS=192.168.1.20:47770
export NYX_BRIDGE_TOKEN=...

docs.title: Running code in a process
docs.text: NyxClient connects to a Nyx bridge server and runs the code it sends.

docs.title: Serving
docs.text:
There are two ways to run it:

from nyx_bridge.client import NyxClient

client = NyxClient(name="my-script")

client.serve_forever()                 # blocks; the calling thread executes the code
thread = client.start_in_thread()      # returns a daemon thread; code runs there
  • serve_forever() suits batch applications with no event loop (mayapy, blender --background, a plain script). It returns when the client is stopped, the server asks it to shut down, or reconnecting is off and the connection ends.
  • start_in_thread() serves from a background thread, for applications that keep running their own loop. Anything the application only allows from its main thread needs run_on_main_thread.

client.stop() ends either, and is safe to call from any thread.

docs.title: Constructor
docs.text:
Argument Meaning name Name the server shows. <kind>-<pid> when omitted. address "host:port" or (host, port). See Finding the server. token Server token. From the environment or the address file when omitted. reconnect Connect again when the connection drops (default True). reconnect_delay Seconds between connection attempts (default 1.0).

serve_forever(connect_timeout=None) keeps trying to reach the server until it works. Give a number of seconds to give up with ConnectionError instead. A server that refuses the client (wrong token, wrong protocol version) raises protocol.HandshakeError straight away, since retrying would not help.

docs.title: What a script sees
docs.text:
Code runs in a namespace that lives as long as the connection, so one execution sees the variables of the previous one. The server picks the mode:

  • exec (default): the value of the request is whatever the code assigned to result. result is cleared before each run, so it never carries over.
  • eval: the value is that of a single expression.

Output printed to stdout and stderr is captured and sent back. Names passed as args are set in the namespace first. A script that calls sys.exit() does not stop the client; it is reported as an error of that execution.

Values travel as JSON. Lists, dicts, strings, numbers, booleans and None arrive as they are, tuples and sets become lists, and anything else (an object of the application) becomes its repr().

# what the server sends...
session.execute("import math\nresult = math.sqrt(x)", args={"x": 16})   # value 4.0
session.execute("math.sqrt(2)", mode="eval")                              # math is still imported

Executions on one client run one at a time, in the order received, even when the server sent several at once.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: execute never raises on the client side. An exception in the code is sent back with its type, message and traceback, and the server re-raises it as RemoteExecutionError. The client keeps working afterwards.

docs.title: Subclassing for an application
docs.text:
Subclass NyxClient for an application and override what differs:

import bpy

from nyx_bridge.client import NyxClient


class BlenderClient(NyxClient):
    CLIENT_KIND = "blender"

    def client_version(self) -> str:
        return bpy.app.version_string

    def default_namespace(self) -> dict:
        return {"bpy": bpy}

    def run_on_main_thread(self, func):
        ...  # queue func for the main thread, wait for and return its result
Member Purpose CLIENT_KIND Label the server can filter on ("blender", "maya"). Default "python". client_version() Version string of the application, sent in the hello. default_namespace() Names every fresh namespace starts with. run_on_main_thread(func) Run func where the application allows its API to be used and return the result. Default runs it on the serving thread. on_connected() / on_disconnected() Called after the handshake and after the connection ended.

run_on_main_thread receives every execution when serving from start_in_thread. A typical implementation puts func on a queue that a timer on the main thread drains, and waits for the result. See nyx-bridge-blender and nyx-bridge-maya for working versions.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text: The client logs to nyx_bridge.client: connections at INFO, failed attempts at DEBUG.

docs.title: Sending code from a server
docs.text:
BridgeServer accepts clients and gives you a ClientSession for each one.

from nyx_bridge.server import BridgeServer

server = BridgeServer(name="my-server")
server.start()
print(server.port, server.token)

session = server.wait_for_client(kind="blender", timeout=60)
result = session.execute("result = len(bpy.data.objects)")
print(result.value, result.stdout)

server.stop()

The server is also a context manager: with BridgeServer() as server: starts it and stops it on exit. start() is a no-op on a running server, and a stopped server can be started again.

docs.title: Constructor
docs.text:
Argument Meaning name Server name, shown to clients. The class name when omitted. host Interface to listen on (default 127.0.0.1). A warning is logged for anything but a local address. port None: try DEFAULT_PORT (47770) and the 20 ports after it. 0: let the system choose. Anything else is used as is. token Shared secret clients must present. Random when omitted. address_file File telling clients where the server is. Written on start(), removed on stop(). See Finding the server.

Warning

Whoever holds the token can have code run in every connected client. Keep the host local and treat the token, and the address file that contains it, as a secret.

If no port can be bound, start() raises OSError.

docs.title: Finding clients
docs.text:
server.clients                              # connected sessions, in order of connection
server.find_clients(kind="maya")            # filter by name, kind and/or client_id
server.wait_for_client(name="shot-010", timeout=30)

wait_for_client returns the first match, waiting until one connects. It raises TimeoutError when none does in time, and RuntimeError if the server is stopped while waiting. Criteria left out match anything.

A ClientSession has id, name, kind, version, address and is_connected.

docs.title: Executing
docs.text:
result = session.execute(
    "result = [o.name for o in bpy.data.objects if o.type == kind]",
    args={"kind": "MESH"},     # set in the client's namespace first (JSON only)
    timeout=10,
)
result.value     # what the code assigned to `result`
result.stdout    # what it printed
result.stderr

mode="eval" evaluates one expression instead of running statements. Several threads can call execute on one session; each gets its own answer, although the client runs them one at a time. See what a script sees for the namespace and value rules.

session.ping(timeout=5.0) checks the client answers. session.request_shutdown() asks it to disconnect and stop without reconnecting. session.close() drops the connection.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Raised When RemoteExecutionError The code raised in the client. Has type_name, message, remote_traceback, stdout and stderr. ClientDisconnected The client is gone, or went away while you waited. A subclass of ConnectionError. TimeoutError No answer within timeout. A late answer is ignored. TypeError args can't be serialized to JSON. Raised before anything is sent. 
from nyx_bridge.server import RemoteExecutionError

try:
    session.execute("1 / 0")
except RemoteExecutionError as err:
    print(err.type_name, err.message)     # ZeroDivisionError division by zero
    print(err.remote_traceback)

docs.title: Listeners
docs.text:
To follow the server, for a UI for instance, add a listener: any object with some of these methods (the others are skipped).

class Watcher:
    def on_server_started(self, server): ...
    def on_server_stopped(self, server): ...
    def on_client_connected(self, server, session): ...
    def on_client_disconnected(self, server, session): ...

server.add_listener(Watcher())

They run on the server's own threads, so keep them quick and thread safe. A listener that raises is logged and does not affect the server or the other listeners. remove_listener takes one away.

docs.title: Deciding who may connect
docs.text:
The token is checked first. To add your own rule, subclass and override validate_client, returning a reason to refuse or None to accept:

class OnlyKnownKinds(BridgeServer):
    def validate_client(self, hello):
        if hello.get("client_kind") not in {"blender", "maya"}:
            return "unknown client kind"

DEFAULT_PORT, PORT_FALLBACK_COUNT and HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT (seconds a new connection has to send its hello, default 5) are class attributes you can override the same way.
